descriptions.item-and-process-group: Items and the process groups their operations and SMV are filed under.
descriptions.floor-wise-target-setup: How target is derived per floor — the basis every line target is set on.
descriptions.finishing-floor-access-setup: Which users may post against which finishing floor.
descriptions.learning-curve-model: Efficiency ramp expected from a line over the days after a style change.
descriptions.responsible-owner-mapping: The department and the person answerable for each IE activity.
descriptions.resource-capability-profile: Manpower and machine profile of a line — what it holds before it is loaded.

parts.hint: A part may appear on many items. The part library itself is maintained on the Garments Part screen.
parts.item_hint: An item sits in a group — Knit Tops, Bottoms … — and its parts are mapped on the Records tab.

target.hint: Which floors each user may set targets and products on, and with what right. Add a line, tag its floors, and save the grid.
target.footer: :count permission(s). A user appears once. Tag every floor they answer for on the same line — an admin sees them all whatever the tags say.

finishing.hint: Which finishing floors a user may post against, one line per node. Add a line, tag its floors, and save the grid.
finishing.footer: :count grants. Iron and Poly are granted separately — the same user takes a line for each.

curve.hint: Expected efficiency on each day of a style run. Pick a fabric class; the criticality bands are the rows.
curve.footer: :count bands. Blank a cell to drop that day from the curve. Efficiency is a percentage — above 100 is refused.
curve.new_hint: One row per day rather than ten fixed columns, so a factory that runs a fourteen-day curve needs no schema change.
curve.day_hint: 1 is the first day of the run.

owner.title: Responsible Person
owner.hint: Who answers for the selected department, over which floors and which buyer accounts.
owner.empty: Its mappings load beside it, and nothing is read from the database until you do.
owner.footer: :count mapping(s). All-floors and all-buyers are stored rather than inferred from an empty list, so 'everyone' and 'not filled in yet' stay apart.

profile.machine_hint: Leave Machine Type blank for the line's overall manpower establishment.
profile.lines_hint: Which lines may run the selected criticality band, and the garment categories each of those lines is preferred for.
profile.empty: Its lines load beside it, and nothing is read from the database until you do.
profile.footer: :count lines. A line left unticked is not refused work — it is simply not preferred for this band, and the loading board says so.
profile.no_lines: Add lines on Capacity Planning's Line Master first.

grid.empty_text: Add the first one with Add above, then Save.

master.in_use: This item has parts mapped to it; remove them first.
master.part_taken: This part is already mapped to the item.
master.day_taken: This curve already has a point for that day.
master.profile_taken: This line already has a profile for that machine type.
master.line_needs_floor: Every line needs at least one floor.
master.node_once: A user takes one line per node.
master.person_taken: This person already answers for the department.
master.efficiency_max: Efficiency is a percentage — above 100 is refused.

descriptions.gmt-item-specification-entry: Garment item specifications keyed in against a style.
descriptions.gmt-item-specification: The garment item specification register the entry screen writes into.

f.title: Garments Item Specification
f.hint: Pick a variation to edit it, or fill the form to engineer one. The grids are the process groups it is specified against and the machines it needs.
f.existing_help: Choose one to load it back into the form, or leave blank to create.
f.variation_help: The printed screen's numbered tabs — one per engineered variation of the style.
f.nature_help: Left blank, the nature follows the sewing SMV.
f.ob_placeholder: Path or link, or attach a file
f.ob_help: The operation bulletin this SMV was read off. Attaching a file replaces the one on the specification.
f.tech_hint: What the specification says about each process group — the stitch, the trim, the finish the group is worked to.
f.no_process: No process group specified yet. A specification may be saved without one and added to later.
f.mc_hint: How many of each machine type the line needs to run this style.
f.no_machine: No machine required yet. A style with no machine requirement cannot be laid out on a line.
f.foot: Efficiency is a percentage and is capped at 100 — a line cannot beat its own standard minute. The OB file is attached from this machine and stored with the specification.
f.records_title: Engineered style specifications with manpower, SMV, efficiency and machines

list.title: GMT Item List
list.print_hint: Order items with the specification their style carries, as filtered on screen.
list.empty: No item matches the boxes above. Widen the month, the buyer or the item.
list.foot: CM/Dz and BgtExp% are the rate quoted against the style's specification for the booking month, on Item Spec Wise CM. An item with no specification yet prints zeroes and a status saying so.

var.title: Gmt Tech Variations
var.hint: Pick a category; its technical variations are the rows. Add a line, type the SMV each order-quantity band attracts, and save the grid.
var.empty: Its variations load beside it, and nothing is read from the database until you do.
var.footer: :count variations. Every line needs a technical specification. The bands are the printed order-quantity ranges; each holds the SMV that quantity attracts.
var.records_title: Technical variations by category, with the SMV each order-quantity band attracts

grp.name: Itm Group
grp.title: Itm Category
grp.hint: The garment item register. Pick a group to see its categories; add a group beside the list, or a category on the grid.
grp.empty: Its categories load beside it, and nothing is read from the database until you do.
grp.footer: :count categorys. A category quoted on a tech variation or a component mapping cannot be removed — withdraw it by clearing Active instead.

v.group_taken: There is already a group by that name.
v.smv: Sewing SMV must be greater than zero.
v.efficiency: Efficiency is a percentage and is capped at 100.
v.category_taken: This category is already in the group.
v.category_in_use: :name is quoted on a tech variation or a component mapping — clear Active instead.

descriptions.item-spec-wise-cm: Cost of making worked out per item specification.
descriptions.oh-cost-allocation: Overhead spread across sections on an agreed basis.
descriptions.daily-line-costing-operation: What a line cost to run today, against what it produced.

cm.title: New CM rate
cm.hint: One CM per specification per booking month.

head.title: New cost head
head.hint: The cost heads are the particulars maintained on the Section Cost Heads tab. Where the money goes is typed on the Monthly Cost Re-arrange sheet, a whole month at a time.
head.head: Cost Head
head.work_days_help: Only the section's first line carries it on the printed sheet. Left blank, the sheet reads the line above.

sec.title: Monthly OP + ASO Salary & OT Rate
sec.hint: The particulars each section is costed against. Pick a section, add its heads, and save the list.
sec.name: Particulars Name-EN
sec.f_target: Money may be re-arranged into it?
sec.f_target_help: A production section the sheet's columns write into. The columns themselves are the six the printed sheet carries.
sec.empty: Its cost heads load beside it, and nothing is read from the database until you do.
sec.footer: :count cost heads. A head with figures on a month stays — clear Active instead of removing it.

sheet.title: Monthly Cost Re-arrange
sheet.hint: Every section's cost heads for one company and month, what each cost, and how the money is re-arranged across the production sections.
sheet.copy_help: Builds the grid from that month's figures instead of this one's. Nothing is written until Save.
sheet.pick_title: Choose a company, a year and a month, then press Show.
sheet.pick: Fill in the panel above and press Show.
sheet.footer: Choose a company, a year and a month, then press Show. The rows are the particulars maintained on the Section Cost Heads tab — add one there and it appears here the next month as well as this one. Copy From leaves the grid unsaved: Save Sheet is what commits it, and always into the month chosen above.
sheet.no_years: No records to choose from yet.

day.pick_title: Choose a floor and a date, then press Refresh.
day.pick: Fill in the panel above and press Refresh.
day.config_hint: The SMV, FOB and per-piece rates every order loaded on one floor is costed at for one day.
day.config_footer: The rows are the orders the target-setting sheet has loaded on this floor today, plus any already costed here. An order costed at nothing throughout is removed when the sheet is saved.
day.lines_hint: What every line on one floor produced in one day, split by the overtime tier it was made in, with the man-minutes of overtime behind it.
day.lines_footer: OP, ASO, WH and Target are filled in from the morning's target-setting sheet; type over them only where the day actually differed. Prod[Total] and Man OT[Total] are added up as you type and are never entered.
day.profit_hint: What each line on one floor earned in CM against what its labour and its share of overhead cost, general hours and each overtime tier apart.
day.profit_footer: Every figure is derived — from Order Config Data, Line Wise Prod, the month's OP+ASO Sal & OT Rate, and the overhead re-arranged on OH Cost Allocation. A line showing no earning is usually a line whose order was never costed on the first tab. Overhead is shared by the lines that ran that day and then follows each line's output across the tiers.
day.no_rate: no salary rate for the month
day.no_prod: No production is recorded for that floor and date. Fill in the Line Wise Prod tab first.
day.empty_orders: No order is loaded on this floor for that date.
day.new_hint: One row per order per floor per day.

v.cm_taken: This specification already has a CM rate for that booking month.
v.ship_after: Ship Date cannot be before the Confirm Date.
v.section_in_use: This section has cost heads — remove them first.
v.head: Cost Head is required.
v.head_taken: This cost head already has a line for that month — change it on the sheet.
v.expense_row: Line :n is re-arranged but has no Monthly Expense.
v.head_in_use: :head has figures on a month — clear Active instead.
v.order_taken: This order is already costed on that floor for that day.
v.smv: SMV must be greater than zero.
v.line_order: Line :n produced pieces but names no order.

descriptions.ot-plan-garment-division: Overtime planned across the garment division, floor by floor.
descriptions.monthly-op-aso-salary-ot-rate: Operator and ASO salary and overtime rates the month is costed at.

new.title: New OT plan row
new.hint: Operators and ASOs are planned separately per hour because they are paid at different rates.
new.hour_help: Creates that many hour rows from 6PM, each holding its own operator and ASO count.

plan.title: OT Plan
plan.hint: Every manpower group posted to one floor, and how many operators and ASOs of each are planned to stay to each hour between 6PM and 5AM.
plan.footer: MP.(Gen.) is the headcount posted to the group and is filled in for you; type over it only when the plan covers a different number. A group planned at no hours writes nothing, so a plan is withdrawn by clearing its boxes.
plan.empty: No manpower group is posted to this floor or planned for that day.

rate.title: Cost Particulars
rate.hint: One company's operator and ASO average salary and overtime rate, month by month, for the year chosen above.
rate.pick_title: Choose a company and a year, then press Show.
rate.pick: Fill in the panel above and press Show.
rate.footer: Every month is on the sheet whether or not it has been costed. A month left at zero throughout is removed from the register when the sheet is saved, so a year is corrected by clearing it rather than by deleting rows one at a time.
rate.new_hint: These rates are what the line costing screens value an OT hour at.

v.rates_month: :month needs all four rates, or none.
v.month_taken: That month already has its rates — change them on Cost Particulars.
v.hours: OT Hours to Plan is required.
v.hours_max: At most :n hours can be planned.
v.per_hour: Plan at least one operator or ASO per hour.
v.group_taken: That group already has a plan for this floor and day — change it on the OT Plan sheet.
v.more_than_mp: Group :n plans more people for an hour than its MP.(Gen.).

descriptions.excess-yarn-target: The yarn overrun a style is allowed before it is costed back.
descriptions.style-feeding-sco: Styles fed to a line and the change-over booked between one and the next.
descriptions.gmt-target-setting: Hourly and daily garment target set per line and style.

yarn.title: Excess Yarn Target
yarn.hint: The yarn overrun each department is allowed in one company's month. Choose the month — or copy another one across — and save the grid.
yarn.copy_help: Builds the grid from that month's figures instead of this one's. Nothing is written until Save.
yarn.pick_title: Choose a company and a month, then press Show.
yarn.footer: Clear a cell to drop that department's target for the month — a blank is no allowance agreed, which is not the same as an allowance of zero. Copy From leaves the grid unsaved: Save Target is what commits it.
yarn.new_hint: The allowance one department gets for one month.

sco.title: Style Changeover Dashboard
sco.hint: Change-overs by floor, line, buyer and style over a date range. Tick the rows to finalise or remove them.
sco.pick_title: Choose a range, then press Search.
sco.pick: Fill in the panel above and press Search.
sco.empty: No change-over was booked in that range.
sco.summary: :count change-over(s) · :minutes minute(s) lost · :open not finalised · :ticked row(s) ticked
sco.footer: Finalising is what makes the efficiency report deduct a change-over's lost minutes. A finalised row can be reopened, but not removed.

new.hint: A line moving from one style to the next, and the minutes it cost.

sheet.title: Sewing Target Setting
sheet.hint: Every line on one floor and every order it is running, with the manpower, work hours and efficiency each target is worked out from.
sheet.copy_help: Start Copy brings that day's setup onto this one — order, SMV, manpower, hours and efficiency, with the production left at nothing. Lines that already have an order today are left alone.
sheet.summary: :date · :lines line(s) · :orders order(s) set · uOP :op[:lop] · uASO :aso[:laso] · Target :target · Achiv :prod · InputMin :imin · ProdMin :pmin · Value :value
sheet.footer: Target[Gen Hr] is worked out from Used OP + ASO, WH, T.Effi. and SMV when the sheet is saved — it is never typed. Every line carries one spare row for a second order: fill it in and save, and the next Refresh offers another. A row left blank writes nothing, and clearing a saved row removes it.

entry.title: Production Entry
entry.hint: Every order allocated to one line, when it is planned to run, and how many pieces the line has made against each allocation.
entry.footer: Production is the running total against the allocation, not the day's output — the day's output is on the target sheet. The spare rows at the bottom allocate a new order to this line; a plan added here runs from the start of the day it names, and its hours can be set on the register.

plans.title: Production Plans
plans.hint: The same allocations read the other way round: which are on today's target, how each stands, and what the line is loaded and un-loaded by.
plans.summary: :line · :plans plan(s), :on on target · Allocation :alloc · Load :load · Un-Load :unload (:pct%)
plans.footer: In Trgt? is what puts a plan on the day's target sheet. Closing a plan takes it off the sheet and stops further production against it; a closed plan re-opened keeps everything already made. Allocation and Production are entered on Production Entry, not here.
plans.empty: No order is allocated to this line yet.

npt.title: NPT Entry
npt.hint: The non-productive time booked against one line for one day — what stopped it, for how long, and which department answers for it.
npt.footer: NPT is manpower x -Min and is worked out when the sheet is saved. A row left blank writes nothing; clearing a saved row removes it. The same hour may be booked to more than one cause — a machine down while the trims were also short is two rows, not a choice between them.

tf.pick_line_title: Choose a floor and a line, then press Refresh.
tf.pick_npt_title: Choose a floor, a date and a line, then press Refresh.

new.title: New sewing target
new.hint: One order on one line for one day; its Target[Gen Hr] is worked out when it is saved.

v.yarn_taken: That department already has a target for this month — change it on the Excess Yarn Target sheet.
v.finalized: A finalised change-over can be reopened, but not removed.
v.wh_range: WH Range To cannot be before WH Range From.
v.smv_row: Line :line has an order without an SMV — SMV must be greater than zero.
v.copy_from: Choose another day to copy from.
v.alloc_order: Row :n is allocated without an Order/Style.
v.npt_slots: Row :n needs at least one hours slot.

descriptions.sewing-prod-adjustment: Corrections booked against a line's recorded sewing output.
descriptions.gmt-wash-requisition: Garments sent out for wash, raised against a style.
descriptions.man-minutes-adjustment: The manpower a line carried but did not sew its order with, hour by hour.

output.title: Sewing Prod Adjustment
output.hint: Every line on one floor for one hour of one day, with the production figure the system recorded beside the figure it is corrected to.
output.pick_title: Choose a floor, a date and an hour, then press Refresh.
output.footer: Prod is what the hour is corrected to. A line left at the recorded figure writes nothing, and a line corrected to the recorded figure again removes the adjustment — so a correction made by mistake is undone by retyping the original, not by hunting for the row.

output_new.title: New production adjustment
output_new.hint: The recorded figure is kept beside the adjusted one — an adjustment that erased what it replaced would not be auditable.

wash.title: Wash Requisition List
wash.hint: Every garment wash requisition with the step it is at, and the action that moves it to the next one.
wash.footer: Take Action moves a requisition one step; leaving it where it is writes nothing. A complete requisition offers no action — it is finished, and the only thing left to do with it is print it.
wash.pick: Fill in the panel above and press Search.
wash.nothing: Choose an action on at least one requisition.

wash_new.title: New wash requisition
wash_new.hint: The requisition number is generated on save.

mm.title: Man Minutes Adjustment
mm.hint: Every reason a line's people were not sewing its order, with how many operators and ASOs each took, in the general shift and each overtime hour.
mm.pick_title: Choose a floor, a date and a line, then press Refresh.
mm.footer: Man OT is added up across the nine overtime hours and is never entered. A reason left at nothing writes nothing, so an adjustment is withdrawn by clearing its boxes. The hours are the same nine the OT Plan uses.
mm.summary: :line · :date · :reasons reason(s) · :op OP and :aso ASO booked away

mm_new.title: New man-minute adjustment
mm_new.hint: The general-shift figures are entered here; the overtime hours behind them are filled in on the sheet, which prints every reason for a line at once.

v.unchanged: Prod (adjusted) is the recorded figure — there is nothing to correct.
v.output_taken: That line already has an adjustment for this hour — change it on the Sewing Prod Adjustment sheet.
v.close_date: Close Date cannot be before Start Date.
v.wash_missing: That requisition is no longer there — search again.
v.wash_complete: :no is complete — it has no action left.
v.mm_taken: That line already has this reason for the day — change it on the Man Minutes Adjustment sheet.
v.mm_nobody: Book at least one operator or ASO away.

descriptions.sec-wise-profit-loss-config: How each section's profit and loss is composed before it is run.
descriptions.sec-wise-profit-loss-trans: The section-wise profit and loss itself, posted for the period.

cfg.title: Income Target Config
cfg.hint: What each section is set to produce in a month, the rate it is worth, and the income that comes to.
cfg.copy_help: Update writes that month's figures onto this one. Sections already set here are left alone.
cfg.pick_title: Choose a company, a year and a month, then press Show.
cfg.pick: Fill in the panel above and press Show.
cfg.footer: Target Income is daily target x Avg Rate x WrkDay/Mn and is worked out when the sheet is saved — it is never typed. A section left at nothing writes nothing, so a section that carries no production target simply stays blank. Update brings another month's figures onto this one without overwriting a section already set here.

cfg_new.title: New income target
cfg_new.hint: Target income is derived from daily target × rate × working days — it is not typed.

trans.title: SecWise Profit/Loss-Trans
trans.hint: What each section earned on one day for one company, against what it was targeted at and what it cost to earn.
trans.pick_title: Choose a company and a date, then press Refresh.
trans.pick: Fill in the panel above and press Refresh.
trans.footer: IncomeTarget and Prod Target open at the section's share of the month set on Income Target Config — type over them only where the day genuinely differed. Profit/Loss is Income less overhead, material and expense, and is never entered. A section left at nothing writes nothing.

trans_new.title: New section result
trans_new.hint: Profit or loss is derived on read from income less the three costs, so the column can never contradict them.

v.target_rate: Daily production target and average rate are both required.
v.target_taken: That section already has a target for this month — change it on the Income Target Config sheet.
v.result_taken: That section already has a result for this day — change it on the SecWise Profit/Loss-Trans sheet.
v.rate_row: :section has a daily target without an Avg Rate — both are required.
v.copy_from: Choose another month to copy from.

descriptions.ie-reports: The module's report set — SMV, line balancing, efficiency and costing.

rp.result_hint: Read from Work Study's own sheets at the moment Preview was pressed.
rp.empty: No rows for this report and these parameters.

pending.garments: This report reads sewing input, output and WIP, which Garments Production records. It runs once that module is built.
pending.attendance: This report reads who came to work and stayed, which HR & Payroll attendance records. It runs once attendance is built.
pending.layout: This report reads line layouts and balancing, which the Assembly Floor records. It runs once that module is built.
pending.booking: This report reads capacity booking against orders. It runs once the booking side of Capacity Planning is built.
pending.print: This report reads print and embroidery costing. It runs once the Printing and Embroidery modules are built.
pending.accounts: This report reads the factory's cost per minute from Finance & Ledger. It runs once that is built.

report.input_output_wip: Date Wise Input, Output & WIP Report
report.line_plan_actual: Line Wise Plan + Actual Prod With Value
report.floor_plan_value: Floor Wise Plan Prod with Value
report.plan_target_input: Date Wise Plan Vs Target Vs Input Vs Production
report.target_gen_ot: Target & Achv In Gen and OT Hour
report.planning_vs_ie: Planning Vs IE Target Vs Production Summary
report.ot_plan_actual: OT Plan vs Actual- Garment Division

run.title: New report run
run.hint: The report catalogue is data, not a hard-coded list — a report can be added or retired without a deployment.

v.range: To Date cannot be before From Date.
